learning_outcomes.text: The learner can obtain information, ideas and opinions from highly specialised sources within their field, and understand specialised articles outside their field, provided they use a dictionary occasionally to confirm their interpretation of terminology.

The learner can read with a large degree of independence, adapting style and speed of reading to different texts and purposes, and using appropriate reference sources selectively, and has a broad active reading vocabulary, but may experience some difficulty with low-frequency idioms.

The learner can understand standard language or a familiar variety, live or broadcast, on both familiar and unfamiliar topics normally encountered in personal, social, academic or vocational life. Only extreme background noise, inadequate discourse structure and/or idiomatic usage influence the ability to understand.

The learner can understand the main ideas of propositionally and linguistically complex discourse on both concrete and abstract topics delivered in standard language or a familiar variety, including technical discussions in their field of specialisation.

The learner can give clear, detailed descriptions and presentations on a wide range of subjects related to their field of interest and develop meaningful conversations or monologues on them, expanding and supporting ideas with subsidiary points and relevant examples.

The learner can produce clear, detailed texts on a variety of subjects related to their field of interest, synthesising and evaluating information and arguments from a number of sources; have no difficulty employing a wide range of grammatical structures.
The learner can maintain a generally high level of lexical accuracy; understand and use much of the specialist vocabulary of their field.
The learner can show a relatively high degree of grammatical control without making mistakes which lead to misunderstanding.

syllabus_topics: Modals for advice, permission, and obligation; Modals in the past and present; have got to; Polite requests and offers; Using sequencers in instructions.

Present Perfect (Simple, continuous, passive & Time expressions); Verbs and adverbs that go together; Adverbs without -ly; Have you ever … ?, How long … ?; Numbers; Using adverbs in descriptive writing.

Future forms: will, going to or Present Continuous; may, might, could for future possibility; Prefixes, Suffixes; Making arrangements.

assessment_rules: The overall grade is calculated from 50% Final Exam and 50% in-term achievement. The in-term achievement is based on Quiz 1 (15%), Quiz 2 (15%) and Midterm Exam 1 (70%).
